name: knowledge_holdout
purpose: HOLD-OUT evaluation of query_knowledge. Real questions an AI would ask while building a game with these tools, in the words of someone who has not read the corpus. Graded by the expected CHUNK ID(S): a result counts when its id, or the id of the chunk it was split from (field parent), is in 'expected'. expected=null means the corpus has no chunk that answers it (a GAP): those are reported separately and are NOT part of rank-1 / top-3 / MRR. The 25 first questions are the audit's (GAPS_AND_IMPROVEMENTS_2026-10-23.md, K-07); the rest were written by the same author before any retrieval change.
rules: NEVER tune synonyms, stopwords or weights on this file. Tune on knowledge_dev.json. This file is run for the record (before / after a change), not as a feedback loop.
expected ids were written from the corpus listing and a grep of the text, not from the search results.
A question whose honest answer is 'the corpus does not have it' is a gap (expected null); it is not 'fixed' by loosening the grade, only by writing the chunk.

recorded.note: Run exactly twice for the record, never used for tuning. n = 47 graded questions (5 gaps excluded). Grading is tolerant: 2-6 acceptable chunk ids per question, so these rates are higher than the audit's strict 44% on its 25 questions.

before_2026-10-23.what: mcp rag_query.py (synonyms) on the 377-chunk corpus as it was

after_2026-10-23.what: new rag_query.py (title x4, tags x3, synonyms x0.6, filler words dropped, superseded excluded) on the 437+ chunk corpus (categories merged, stale chunks retired, 17 long chunks split)

recorded.known_limits: A search always returns something: the 5 gap questions (mini map, translate, multiplayer, rebind keys, draw distance for trees) get a confident-looking wrong top hit. No abstention score exists yet.
